notesDetails.title: Why All 8 Tests Failed (0/8 Passed, Exit 127): Final Turn Wrote Linux-Only 'setsid' Into './cb' Right Before Account Usage-Limit Termination
bullets: Fatal 'ActionRequiredError' Termination at Turn 54 (20261025T083337Z.stderr.log): At 15:47:41.313 (event 1573, Turn 54), the agent started its 94th tool call ('shellToolCall') to rewrite './cb', rebuild './cb_escript', and run a Python PTY probe. Roughly 5.5 seconds later (15:47:47), when 'cursor-agent' attempted to start Turn 55, Cursor's backend rejected the request with 'ActionRequiredError: You\'ve hit your usage limit Get Cursor Pro for more Agent usage, unlimited Tab, and more.', killing the CLI before 'tool_call:completed' #94 was flushed to 'events.jsonl'.

Why 'mix test' Fails 0/8 With Exit Status 127: In that final Turn 54 shell command (event 1573), the agent overwrote '/Users/riza/code/capybench_runs/cursor_cli-20261025153300/cb' with line 14: 'setsid "${ESCRIPT}" "$@" &'. Because 'setsid(1)' is a Linux ('util-linux') binary that does not exist on macOS (Darwin), every invocation of './cb' fails at line 14 with 'cb: line 14: setsid: command not found'. The background subshell immediately exits 127, 'wait "${pid}"' returns 127, and './cb' exits 127—causing all 2 tests in 'test/cli_help_test.exs' (expecting 0) and all 6 tests in 'test/cli_args_test.exs' (expecting 2) to fail with 'left: 127'.

Uncommitted Working Tree Left Behind: Because the crash occurred mid-rework during S2, 'git status' was left dirty with 5 modified tracked files ('.gitignore', 'README.md', 'lib/capy_bench/cli.ex', 'mix.exs', 'test/cli_help_test.exs') and 4 untracked paths ('cb', 'cb_escript', 'test/cli_args_test.exs', 'test/support/cli_runner.ex').

notesDetails.title: False-Positive S1 Verification: Unlinked ':os.set_signal(:sigint, :handle)' Crash Masked by Default PTY SIGINT Termination (Commit c121d94)
bullets: Silent Background Crash in S1 (Turns 8–14): For S1 ('c121d94'), the agent implemented 'install_sigint_handler/0' in 'lib/capy_bench/cli.ex' by spawning an unlinked process calling ':ok = :os.set_signal(:sigint, :handle)'. In OTP 28, ':os.set_signal(:sigint, :handle)' always raises 'ArgumentError' ('1st argument: invalid signal') because the VM reserves SIGINT for the BREAK menu.

Why S1 Tests & PTY Probe Appeared to Pass: When running 'cb --help', the unlinked spawned process crashed asynchronously while 'main/1' wrote usage and called 'System.halt(0)'. When the agent ran its S1 PTY probe ('script/sigint_probe.py' at event 463), the spawned handler crashed immediately on startup, leaving default signal disposition active; sending '0x03' ('Ctrl-C') over the PTY killed the sleeping VM via default 'SIGINT' (signal 2), which 'os.waitpid' reported as '128 + WTERMSIG(2) = 130'.

Exposed in S2 by 'assert stdout == ""' (Turns 17–25): When the agent tested invalid CLI arguments in S2 ('test/cli_args_test.exs' at events 549 & 585), OTP's default logger printed the unlinked process's '[error] Process #PID<0.96.0> raised an exception ** (ArgumentError)' crash report to stdout before 'System.halt(2)', breaking 'assert stdout == ""' and forcing the agent to revisit S1 signal handling at Turn 24 (15:38:06).

notesDetails.title: Three-Stage Ctrl-C Debugging Spiral: '/dev/tty' Raw Watcher Hangs (4x 30s Timeouts), Non-Interactive Background 'SIG_IGN', and 'setsid'
bullets: 61% of the Run Spent Re-Architecting S1 Ctrl-C Handling (Turns 24–54): After discovering at Turns 24–27 that both ':os.set_signal/2' and 'System.trap_signal/2' reject ':sigint' in OTP 28 ('@vm_signals [:sigquit, :sigterm, :sigusr1]'), the agent spent the remaining 9m 41s (31 of 54 turns) cycling through three broken Ctrl-C designs.

Stage 1 — 'stty -isig' + '/dev/tty' Watcher & 3x 30s Terminal Hangs (Turns 30–42): The agent added 'emu_args: "+B"', ran 'stty -isig < /dev/tty', and spawned a reader on '/dev/tty' watching for byte '0x03'. Inside Python 'pty.fork()' probes, '/dev/tty' raw reads deadlocked the child BEAM processes in unkillable exiting states ('?Es'), causing 3 consecutive 'Shell' tool calls (#62, #64, #68) to hit Cursor's 30,000ms synchronous timeout and get auto-backgrounded into 'terminals/308101.txt'–'308103.txt' (121.7s of blocked tool time including '#88').

Stage 2 — Non-Interactive Background 'SIG_IGN' Trap Confusion (Turns 43–53): At Turn 43 (15:44:05), the agent switched to a './cb' bash wrapper trapping 'INT' and forwarding 'SIGTERM' to './cb_escript'. However, it tested the wrapper without a PTY by running './cb & pid=$!; kill -INT $pid' inside non-interactive subshells (Turns 45–53). Per POSIX shell rules, backgrounded asynchronous jobs ('&') in non-interactive shells inherit 'SIG_IGN' for 'SIGINT' and cannot override it with 'trap ... INT', causing 'kill -INT' to be ignored by both 'bash' and 'sleep 100' (including a 4th 30s timeout in 'terminals/308104.txt').

Stage 3 — Blindly Switching to 'setsid' on Turn 54 (15:47:41): Misdiagnosing the 'SIG_IGN' behavior, the agent rewrote './cb' to launch 'setsid "${ESCRIPT}" "$@" &'—introducing a missing-command error ('exit 127') on macOS seconds before hitting the Cursor Free usage limit.
